title: The 5-Beat Arc
primitive: arc completeness (hook / setup / rising / turn / close)
summary: A 60-to-120-second told tale has a shape — Hook, Setup, Rising, Turn, Close. This kit listens for whether the shape was complete: did the turn turn? did the close close?

questions.prompt: Listen back to your tale. Where was your TURN? Is it a moment where the meaning rotates — or just a louder version of the same moment?
Which version is a TURN, not just a louder middle?
options: I ran faster, and then faster, and then faster.
I had been running away the whole time — and at the fence, I realized I was running toward.
questions.rationale: A true turn rotates the meaning. The kid wasn't running away; they were running toward. That's a 180. Pivot's head rotates.

questions.prompt: Did your Close try to wrap everything up with a lesson? Or did it land on one specific image and stop? Which felt more honest?
Take a tale that ends 'and that's why you should always be honest.' Replace the moral with a single concrete image that lets the listener feel what you mean.

castCameos.line: My head rotated. The turn landed. The story turned. The listener turned.
Your hook promised a turn. You delivered. The body tipped forward twice.
Turn sharpens. You let the pace tighten right before it. That's why it cut.
If the close echoes a phrase from the hook, the arc closes itself. Try it.
